paragraphs: Friend, this whole passage is God handing out an inheritance, and He does it on purpose, with every border spelled out. He says He swore with an uplifted hand to give this land to their forefathers (Ezekiel 47:14). So the land is not something Israel earned. It is a promise God keeps, down to the last boundary line.

Now look at who gets a place. God says the foreigners who live among them are to be treated as "native-born Israelites" and are allotted an inheritance right in the tribe where they dwell (Ezekiel 47:22-23). No special corner, no second-class section. Then at the center of it all sits the sanctuary of the LORD (Ezekiel 48:8), and the city's twelve gates carry the names of the tribes (Ezekiel 48:31-34). Even Levi, who got no tribal strip, has his name on a gate. I LOVE that.

And then the last line lands: "from that day on the name of the city will be: THE LORD IS THERE." (Ezekiel 48:35). That is the point of the whole vision. God keeps His promises, He makes room for people, and what He wants most is to be with them. Baker, that is why my ovens stay ready, and I will tell you what, I would rather live in a city with that name than in any bakery on earth.
